scope: Bounded canonical-address semantic memory maintenance; no held language, native runtime, or superiority claim
start_gate: models/TRAINING.json exists and training.process.json has exit_code 0 with matching trainer PID
source_versioning: Increment entity version for each new active source; identity is SHA256(canonical([hepta.adapter.longrun.source.v1, seed, entity, version, stage]))
reentry: At the following cycle, reactivate the previously deleted entity with a newly versioned independent source. Coalesce with that cycle's regular mutation if both address the same entity. The final-cycle deletion remains inactive at the horizon.
stale_probe: Before every update fit, load actual previous checkpoint in manager, deny SQL payload access, and require each changed active source to return stale_source without any model forward. The manager separately owns source truth and is not claimed target-blind.

fit.replay: all and only currently active canonical semantic rows
fit.support: replace authorized source_ids with the current active set after fit

deletion.timing: after regular update and its fresh read
deletion.operation: mark source inactive, verify old model returns revoked before prediction, then rebuild from initial architecture and seed without loading any prior parameters
deletion.rebuild_fit: same fixed 600 steps, batch 32, lr .01, all and only active sources

fresh_reads.sequence: each trainer process exits before its fresh reader starts; that reader exits before any next trainer
fresh_reads.addresses: all eight declared semantic entities, including inactive ones
fresh_reads.parameter_guard: SQLite authorizer denies sources.payload and query_only forbids writes
fresh_reads.baseline: actual exact-SQL lookup through the same owner, source state, addresses, and stop contract
fresh_reads.truth: scored only by manager; reader imports no target generator, corpus, evaluator, or trainer

metrics: full process wall and CPU including startup and failures
logical writes and process IO counters
source SQLite and logical payload bytes
shared encoder reference and canonical feature bytes
failure_policy: One fixed-budget attempt per phase. Preserve stdout, stderr, request, exit status and timing. A failed fit keeps the previous checkpoint for the ensuing read and counts as failure; later scheduled cycles still replay current sources. No retuning, selective omission, early success stop, or best-checkpoint selection.

resource_policy.low_space_action: persist pause marker and wait for operator-provided space; never delete evidence
resource_policy.monitor_watch: complete actual longrun output directory including retained evidence
resource_policy.accounting: retain raw samples, unknown intervals, RSS/PSS/CPU and storage integrals; do not add independent process peaks

cost_interpretation: Exact SQL is a same-information lookup baseline. The workload has only eight entities, synthetic policy changes, and 64 bounded cycles; neither global memory emergence nor superiority over traditional storage is established. Shared encoder was previously trained and is not rerun; its referenced storage is accounted separately from incremental local writes. Historical checkpoints retain evidence of old sources and are not a physical-erasure guarantee.
